nahhas-irab:36-36.t: فَلَمَّا جاءَ سُلَيْمانَ قالَ أَتُمِدُّونَنِ بِمالٍ: if you wish, you may assimilate (idghām) the nūn into the nūn, and that is permissible, even though it involves bringing two quiescent letters together.

nahhas-irab:37-37.t: فَلَنَأْتِيَنَّهُمْ بِجُنُودٍ لا قِبَلَ لَهُمْ بِها: a lām of oath, and the nūn is necessarily attached to it. Abū Jaʿfar said: I heard Abū al-Ḥasan ibn Kaysān say: it is a lām of emphasis (tawkīd); and likewise his view was that the lāms are all three and no more: the lām of emphasis, the lām of command, and the lām of the genitive (khafḍ). This is the view of the most skilled grammarians, because they return a thing to its origin, and this is only possible for one who is well practised in Arabic. أَذِلَّةً: as a ḥāl (circumstantial). وَهُمْ صاغِرُونَ: also in the position of a ḥāl.

nahhas-irab:38-38.t: It was said: what he meant by this is that if they came as Muslims (in submission), it would not be permissible to bring her throne except with her permission. And it was said: what Solomon ﷺ intended was to display a miraculous sign.

nahhas-irab:39-39.t:
قالَ عِفْرِيتٌ مِنَ الْجِنِّ: Abū Isḥāq said: the ʿifrīt is the one who is effective in affairs and goes to extremes in them, who has malice and cunning. One also says: ʿifr, ʿifāriya and ʿifriya. It is reported from Abū Rajāʾ that he read: قال عفرية من الجنّ. One also says: ʿifriya nifriya, as an itbāʿ (rhyming echo-pairing). Whoever says ʿifriya forms its plural as ʿafārin; and whoever says
ʿifrīt has three options in the plural: if he wishes he says ʿafārīt; if he wishes he says ʿafārin, because the tāʾ is redundant (zāʾida), just as one says ṭawāghin as the plural of ṭāghūt; and if he wishes he compensates for the tāʾ and says:
ʿafāriyy.

nahhas-irab:40-40.t: Al-Akhfash said: the meaning is: that He may see whether I give thanks or am ungrateful. Someone else said: the meaning of «ليبلوني» is «to make me His servant in worship», and it is figurative (majāz).

nahhas-irab:41-41.t: قالَ نَكِّرُوا لَها عَرْشَها: al-Farrāʾ claimed that he only ordered it to be disguised because the devils had told him: there is something wrong in her mind; so he wanted to test her. نَنْظُرْ: jussive (majzūm) because it is the answer to the command; and whoever reads it in the nominative makes it a new, resumptive clause. أَتَهْتَدِي: there are two views on its meaning. One of them: will she be guided to recognising it; and the other: will she be guided by this great sign and know that none brings it except a prophet from Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and so be guided and abandon error.

nahhas-irab:42-42.t:
قالَتْ كَأَنَّهُ هُوَ: the khabar (predicate) of kaʾanna is referred to by a pronoun, because it has already been mentioned. وَأُوتِينَا الْعِلْمَ مِنْ قَبْلِها: it was said:
the knowledge of tawḥīd (the Oneness of Allah). وَكُنَّا مُسْلِمِينَ: it was said: because her people had become Muslims before her.

nahhas-irab:43-43.t:
«ما» may be in the position of the nominative, i.e. her worship apart from Allah and her worship of it prevented her from knowing what we have known, from submitting [Translator's note: so in the text: «عن أن تعلم ما علمناه عن أن تسلم»]. And «ما» may be in the position of the accusative, the implied meaning being: and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, prevented her from her worship — i.e. and Solomon ﷺ prevented her from her worship — so «عن» was omitted and the verb became transitive. Sībawayh recited: [al-Ṭawīl] 321-
ونبئت عبد الله بالجوّ أصبحت ... كراما مواليها لئيما صميمها
(I was told that ʿAbd Allāh in al-Jaww came to have noble clients while its pure stock was base.)
And he claimed that in his view the meaning is «I was told about ʿAbd Allāh». Whoever reads (أنّها) with the hamza vowelled with fatḥa, anna is in the position of the accusative in the sense of «because she»; and it may be a badal (substitute) for «ما». The kasra is on the basis of a new (resumptive) clause.

nahhas-irab:44-44.t:
[Translator's note: the opening words of the quotation are cut off in the text: «لَ لَهَا» for قِيلَ لَهَا.] لَ لَهَا ادْخُلِي الصَّرْحَ
The implied form according to the doctrine of Sībawayh is «ادخلي إلى الصرح»; «إلى» was omitted and the verb was made transitive. Abū al-ʿAbbās [al-Mubarrad] judges him to be in error in this; he said: because «دخل» indicates an object.
[Translator's note: likewise cut off: «لَتْ» for قَالَتْ.] لَتْ رَبِّ إِنِّي ظَلَمْتُ نَفْسِي
Inna is given kasra because it is at the start of a clause after the verb of saying; and some Arabs give it fatḥa, making the verb of saying govern it. أَسْلَمْتُ مَعَ سُلَيْمانَ لِلَّهِ رَبِّ الْعالَمِينَ
If you make [the ʿayn of] «عَ» [i.e. مع] quiescent [Translator's note: the word is truncated in the text as «عَ»],
it is a particle that has come for a meaning, without disagreement among the grammarians. If you give it fatḥa, there are two views: one of them is that it is a noun in the sense of an adverb (ẓarf), and the other that it is a genitive-governing particle, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa.

nahhas-irab:45-45.t: وَلَقَدْ أَرْسَلْنا إِلى ثَمُودَ أَخاهُمْ صالِحاً: it is made a name for the tribe and so is treated as a diptote (not inflected with tanwīn); inflecting it fully is good, taking it as a name for the clan. فَإِذا هُمْ فَرِيقانِ يَخْتَصِمُونَ: according to the meaning; and «يختصمان» would be according to the wording.

nahhas-irab:46-46.t: قالَ يا قَوْمِ لِمَ تَسْتَعْجِلُونَ بِالسَّيِّئَةِ قَبْلَ الْحَسَنَةِ: Abū Isḥāq said: i.e. why did you say: «If what you have brought is true, then bring us the punishment».

nahhas-irab:47-47.t: قالُوا اطَّيَّرْنا بِكَ وَبِمَنْ مَعَكَ: Mujāhid said: i.e. we have taken an evil omen. Abū Isḥāq said: the origin is «تطيّرنا»; the tāʾ was assimilated into the ṭāʾ because it is from its place of articulation, and the connecting alif (alif al-waṣl) was brought in so as not to begin with a quiescent letter; when you join it [to what precedes], you drop it. قالَ طائِرُكُمْ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ: al-Farrāʾ said: he is saying: in the Preserved Tablet with Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is [the cause of] your taking me as an evil omen and your augury; and that is from Allah the Exalted — like His saying طائِرُكُمْ مَعَكُمْ [Yā Sīn: 19], i.e. whatever good or evil there is clings to you; it clings to you and is around your necks.

nahhas-irab:48-48.t:
وَكانَ فِي الْمَدِينَةِ تِسْعَةُ رَهْطٍ: [رهط] is a collective noun (ism jamʿ); its plural is arhuṭ, and the plural of the plural is arāhiṭ.
يُفْسِدُونَ فِي الْأَرْضِ وَلا يُصْلِحُونَ: al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: these nine were the great men of the people of the city. They used to cause corruption and command corruption. They sat beneath a huge rock by a river, and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, overturned it upon them and killed them; «so those are their houses, empty because of the wrong they did».

nahhas-irab:49-49.t: قالُوا تَقاسَمُوا بِاللَّهِ لَنُبَيِّتَنَّهُ وَأَهْلَهُ: this is among the best readings of this word, because those addressed are included in it in both wording and meaning. And if one reads «لتبيّننّه» [Translator's note: so in the text, apparently for «لتبيّتنّه», the second-person reading], those addressed are not included in the wording but are included in the meaning. The reading of Mujāhid is «ليبيّتنّه» with yāʾ. Abū Isḥāq said: لَنُبَيِّتَنَّهُ, i.e. they said «we shall surely attack him by night» while swearing to one another, i.e. making mutual oaths. ثُمَّ لَنَقُولَنَّ لِوَلِيِّهِ ما شَهِدْنا مَهْلِكَ أَهْلِهِ: «مهلك» is in the sense of «destruction» (ihlāk), and it can be in the sense of an adverb (ẓarf). From ʿĀṣim: «ما شهدنا مهتل» [Translator's note: so in the text; probably «مَهْلَك» (mahlak) is intended], in the sense of «perishing» (halāk); and also from him مَهْلِكَ, which is a noun of the place of perishing, as you say: majlis.

nahhas-irab:50-50.t: وَمَكَرُوا مَكْراً: i.e. what they did. وَمَكَرْنا مَكْراً: We requited them for that. And it was said: plotting (makr) on the part of Allah is bringing the deserved punishment from where the servant does not realise.

nahhas-irab:51-51.t: فَانْظُرْ كَيْفَ كانَ عاقِبَةُ مَكْرِهِمْ: the Kufans, al-Ḥasan and Ibn Abī Isḥāq read — and it is the reading of al-Kisāʾī — أَنَّا دَمَّرْناهُمْ with the hamza vowelled with fatḥa. Al-Farrāʾ claimed that its fatḥa comes from two directions: one of them is that you refer it back to «كيف». Abū Jaʿfar said: this does not hold, because «كيف» is interrogative and «أنّا» is not included in the interrogative. The other direction, in his view, is that you repeat «كان» over it, as if you said: «the outcome of their affair was their destruction». Abū Jaʿfar said: this is far-fetched. With the fatḥa there are five aspects: among them, that the implied form is «because We destroyed them», with anna in the position of the accusative; it may be in the position of the nominative as a badal (substitute) for «عاقبة»; it may [Translator's note: the text has «وليجوز», apparently for «ويجوز»] be in the position of the accusative as the khabar of kāna; «عاقبة» may be put in the accusative as the khabar of kāna, with anna in the position of the nominative as the noun (ism) of kāna; and it may be in the position of the nominative with an implied mubtadaʾ (subject), explaining the outcome, the implied form being: «[it is] that We destroyed them» [Translator's note: the text has «من أنّا دمرناهم»; «من» may be a slip for «هو»]. Whoever reads أَنَّا دَمَّرْناهُمْ [Translator's note: printed here with fatḥa, though the context requires the kasra reading «إِنَّا»] makes it a new (resumptive) clause. Abū Ḥātim said: in the codex of Ubayy it is «أن دمّرناهم», confirming its fatḥa.

nahhas-irab:52-52.t: فَتِلْكَ بُيُوتُهُمْ خاوِيَةً بِما ظَلَمُوا: the accusative is as a ḥāl (circumstantial). The nominative is on five aspects [Translator's note: only four are listed in the text]: «بيوتهم» is a badal (substitute) for «تلك» and «خاوية» is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ; or «بيوتهم» is a khabar and «خاوية» a second khabar, as one says: «this is sweet-sour»; or «خاوية» is with an implied mubtadaʾ, i.e. «they are empty»; or it is a badal from «بيوتهم», because an indefinite may be substituted for a definite.

nahhas-irab:54-54.t: وَلُوطاً إِذْ قالَ لِقَوْمِهِ: in the sense of «and We sent Lot», or «and remember Lot».

nahhas-irab:55-55.t: أَإِنَّكُمْ: lightening the second hamza is the choice of al-Khalīl and Sībawayh, may Allah have mercy on them both. As for the writing, the way is to write it with two alifs in all the readings, because it is a hamza at the start of a word, on which the interrogative alif has entered. وَتَأْتُونَ فِي نادِيكُمُ الْمُنْكَرَ [al-ʿAnkabūt: 29]: Mujāhid said: they used to have intercourse with one another in their gatherings.

nahhas-irab:56-56.t: Al-Ḥasan and Ibn Abī Isḥāq read: فَما كانَ جَوابَ قَوْمِهِ إِلَّا أَنْ قالُوا [Translator's note: printed with the accusative «جَوابَ»; by what follows, their reading is «جوابُ» in the nominative]; they made «أن» the khabar of kāna: «and the answer of his people was nothing but their saying». ʿĀṣim read قَدَّرْناها lightened [i.e. «قَدَرْناها»; Translator's note: printed with shadda], and the meaning is the same. One says: qadartu al-shayʾa qadran and qadaran, and qaddartuhu.

nahhas-irab:59-59.t:
قُلِ الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ: al-Farrāʾ said: the meaning is: it was said to Lot ﷺ: «say: praise be to Allah» for their destruction, وَسَلامٌ عَلى عِبادِهِ الَّذِينَ اصْطَفى. A group of scholars disagreed with al-Farrāʾ on this and said: it is an address to our Prophet ﷺ. Abū Jaʿfar said: this is more fitting, because the Qurʾān was sent down to the Prophet ﷺ and everything in it is addressed to him, upon him be peace, except what can only have a correct meaning if [addressed to] someone else. آللَّهُ خَيْرٌ: Abū Ḥātim permitted «أالله» with two hamzas, and we know of no one who followed him in that. This madd was only brought to distinguish between the interrogative and the statement, and this is the alif of «tawqīf» (prompting confirmation). «خير» here is not in the sense of «better than you» (the afʿal form); it is only like the saying of the poet Ḥassān: [al-Wāfir] 322-
فشرّكما لخيركما الفداء
(So let the worse of you two be ransom for the better of you two.)
So the meaning is: the one of you two in whom there is evil is a ransom for the one in whom there is good. It cannot be in the sense of «than» (min), because if you say «so-and-so is worse than so-and-so», then there is evil in each of them.

nahhas-irab:60-60.t: ʿIkrima said: the gardens (ḥadāʾiq) are date-palms. ذاتَ بَهْجَةٍ: the people of tafsīr said: bahja is adornment and beauty.

nahhas-irab:65-65.t: قُلْ لا يَعْلَمُ مَنْ فِي السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ الْغَيْبَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ: Abū Isḥāq said: this is a badal (substitute) for «من», and the meaning is: no one knows the unseen except Allah. He said: and whoever puts it in the accusative does so as an exception (istithnāʾ) — meaning in speech [generally]. Abū Jaʿfar said: I heard him use this verse as proof against anyone who believes an astrologer, and he said: I fear he will become an unbeliever, because of the generality of this verse.

nahhas-irab:66-66.t: بَلِ ادَّارَكَ عِلْمُهُمْ فِي الْآخِرَةِ: this is the reading of most of the grammarians [Translator's note: so in the text; «readers» (al-qurrāʾ) seems intended], among them Shayba, Nāfiʿ, Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb, ʿĀṣim, al-Aʿmash, Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī. Abū Jaʿfar [the reader], Abū ʿAmr, Ibn Kathīr and Ḥumayd read «بل أدرك». ʿAṭāʾ ibn Yasār read «بل أدرك» with the hamza lightened. Ibn Muḥayṣin read «بل أدرك علمهم في الآخرة» [Translator's note: the three readings appear identical in the unvowelled text; the vowelling that distinguished them is lost]. Ibn ʿAbbās read «بلى ادّارك», and its chain of transmission (isnād) is sound: it is from the ḥadīth of Shuʿba from Abū Ḥamza from Ibn ʿAbbās. Hārūn the reader claimed that the reading of Ubayy ibn Kaʿb is «بل تدارك علمهم». The first reading and the last have the same meaning, because the origin of «ادّارك» is «تدارك»: the tāʾ was assimilated into the dāl, and the connecting alif was brought because one cannot begin with a quiescent letter; when you join it, the connecting alif drops, and the lām [of بل] takes kasra because of the meeting of two quiescent letters. On its meaning there are two views. One is that the meaning is: rather their knowledge in the Hereafter became complete, because they saw everything they had been promised with their own eyes, and so their knowledge of it became complete. The other view is that the meaning is: rather their knowledge followed in succession today concerning the Hereafter, so they said: it will be, and they said: it will not be. On the meaning of «أدرك» there are two views: one, that its meaning is «became complete in the Hereafter», which is like the first; and the other, that it carries the meaning of denial, and this is the doctrine of Abū Isḥāq. He adduced as proof of the soundness of this view that it is followed by بَلْ هُمْ مِنْها عَمُونَ. As for the meaning of «أدرك» [Translator's note: presumably the interrogative form «آدّارك/أأدرك» is meant here], it has only one aspect, in which there is the meaning of denial, as you say: «Did I fight you?», i.e. I did not fight you; so the meaning is: it did not attain. بَلْ هُمْ مِنْها عَمُونَ: the yāʾ was dropped from it because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, and it was not permissible to give it a vowel because a vowel is heavy on it.

nahhas-irab:67-67.t:
This is how Nāfiʿ reads in this sūra and in Sūrat «al-ʿAnkabūt». Abū ʿAmr read with two interrogatives, except that he lightened the hamza. ʿĀṣim and Ḥamza also read with two interrogatives, except that they both pronounced the two hamzas fully. Everything we have mentioned in both sūras is the same. Al-Kisāʾī read أَإِذا with two hamzas, and (اننا) with two nūns in this sūra, and in Sūrat «al-ʿAnkabūt» with two interrogatives. The first reading, «إذا كنا ترابا وآباؤنا أننا», agrees with the script and is good. Abū Ḥātim objected to it, and the sense of his words is this: «إذا» is not interrogative, while «أإنا» is interrogative and contains «أنّ»; so how can what is in the domain of the interrogative govern what precedes it, and how can what follows anna govern what precedes it? How could «tomorrow, that Zayd is going out» be permissible? And if there is an interrogative in it, it is even more remote. If one is asked about this, it is a difficulty because of what he mentioned. Abū Jaʿfar said: I heard Muḥammad ibn al-Walīd say: Abū al-ʿAbbās Muḥammad ibn Yazīd [al-Mubarrad] asked us about a verse of the Qurʾān whose i'rab is hard and difficult, namely His saying, Mighty and Majestic: وَقالَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا هَلْ نَدُلُّكُمْ عَلى رَجُلٍ يُنَبِّئُكُمْ إِذا مُزِّقْتُمْ كُلَّ مُمَزَّقٍ إِنَّكُمْ لَفِي خَلْقٍ جَدِيدٍ [Sabaʾ: 7]. He said: if «ينبئكم» governs «إذا», it is absurd, because he does not inform them at that time; and if what comes after inna governs it, the meaning is correct, but it is an error in Arabic for what follows inna to govern what precedes it.
This is a clear question, and it should be discussed in the sūra where it occurs. As for Abū ʿUbayd, he inclined to the reading of Nāfiʿ and rejected those who combine two interrogatives, adducing the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: أَفَإِنْ ماتَ أَوْ قُتِلَ انْقَلَبْتُمْ عَلى أَعْقابِكُمْ [Āl ʿImrān: 144], and His saying, Mighty and Majestic: أَفَإِنْ مِتَّ فَهُمُ الْخالِدُونَ [al-Anbiyāʾ: 34]. This rebuttal of Abū ʿAmr, ʿĀṣim, Ḥamza, Ṭalḥa and al-Aʿraj entails nothing, and the verse he brought does not resemble it at all. The difference between them is that the condition and its apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) are like a single thing: the meaning of أَفَإِنْ مِتَّ فَهُمُ الْخالِدُونَ is «if you die, will they live forever?». A parallel to this is:
«Is Zayd going?» — one does not say «Is Zayd, is going?», because the two are like a single thing. The verse is not like that, because the second is a self-standing clause, so the interrogative is fitting in it, and the first is a separate utterance in which the interrogative is fitting. As for whoever omits the interrogative from the second, [he omits] the interrogative because there is an indication of it in the speech, for the meaning of denial [Translator's note: the final sentence is elliptical in the text].

nahhas-irab:81-81.t: وَما أَنْتَ بِهادِي الْعُمْيِ: this is the reading of the Medinans, Abū ʿAmr, ʿĀṣim and al-Kisāʾī. Al-Farrāʾ and Abū Ḥātim permitted «وما أنت بهاد العمى». Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb, al-Aʿmash and Ḥamza read «وما أنت تهدي العمي عن ضلالتهم», and in the codex of ʿAbd Allāh [ibn Masʿūd]: «وما أن تهدي العمي عن ضلالتهم». The first reading has the yāʾ dropped in pronunciation because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, and kept in the script. The second reading has the yāʾ dropped in pronunciation and in script because it is quiescent and the tanwīn after it is quiescent; some Arabs keep it in pause, saying «marartu bi-qāḍī», because the tanwīn does not remain in pause. The third reading has the yāʾ dropped from it in pronunciation and in connected speech because of the meeting of two quiescent letters. In the codex of ʿAbd Allāh: «وما إن تهدي»: «إن» is redundant (zāʾida) for emphasis, and it restrains «ما» from governing. إِنْ تُسْمِعُ إِلَّا مَنْ يُؤْمِنُ بِآياتِنا: Abū Isḥāq said: i.e. you do not make hear. He said: and the meaning is: you do not make anyone hear so that he takes it in and acts on it, except one who believes in Our signs; as for one who hears and does not accept, he is like the deaf.

nahhas-irab:82-82.t:
وَإِذا وَقَعَ الْقَوْلُ عَلَيْهِمْ: Ḥafṣa daughter of Sīrīn said: I asked Abū al-ʿĀliya about the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: وَإِذا وَقَعَ الْقَوْلُ عَلَيْهِمْ أَخْرَجْنا لَهُمْ دَابَّةً مِنَ الْأَرْضِ, and he said: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed to Noah ﷺ: أَنَّهُ لَنْ يُؤْمِنَ مِنْ قَوْمِكَ إِلَّا مَنْ قَدْ آمَنَ [Hūd: 36] — and it was as though there had been a covering over my face and it was removed. Abū Jaʿfar said: this is an excellent answer, because people are being tested and given respite, since among them are believers and righteous people and those of whom Allah, Mighty and Majestic, knows that they will believe and repent; and for this reason we were commanded to take the jizya. When this ceases, the word becomes due against them and they become like the people of Noah ﷺ when Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said concerning them: أَنَّهُ لَنْ يُؤْمِنَ مِنْ قَوْمِكَ إِلَّا مَنْ قَدْ آمَنَ. أَخْرَجْنا لَهُمْ دَابَّةً مِنَ الْأَرْضِ تُكَلِّمُهُمْ: ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar, Allah's mercy be upon him, said: the Beast will come out of a cleft in al-Ṣafā. Ibn ʿAbbās, ʿIkrima, ʿĀṣim al-Jaḥdarī, Ṭalḥa and Abū Zurʿa read: أَخْرَجْنا لَهُمْ دَابَّةً مِنَ الْأَرْضِ تُكَلِّمُهُمْ [Translator's note: printed with the common vowelling; their reading is «تَكْلِمُهُم» (it wounds/marks them), as the following gloss shows]. ʿIkrima said: i.e. it brands them. On the meaning of «تكلمهم» there are two views; the best that has been said about it is what is reported from Ibn ʿAbbās; he said: by Allah, it both speaks to them (tukallimuhum) and wounds them (taklimuhum): it speaks to the believer, and it wounds the unbeliever or the sinner. Abū Ḥātim said: «تكلّمهم» is as you say «تجرّحهم» (it wounds them repeatedly); he takes it to be an intensive form of «تكلمهم». The Kufans and Ibn Abī Isḥāq read أَنَّ النَّاسَ with the hamza vowelled with fatḥa, and the people of the two Sanctuaries, the people of Syria and the people of Basra read «إن الناس» with the hamza vowelled with kasra. Abū Jaʿfar said: on the fatḥa reading there are two views, and likewise on the kasra reading. Al-Akhfash said: the meaning is «because the people (bi-anna al-nās)». Abū ʿUbayd said:
its position is accusative because the verb falls on it, i.e. «it informs them that the people…». Al-Kisāʾī and al-Farrāʾ said:
«إن الناس» with kasra is on the basis of a new (resumptive) clause. Al-Akhfash said: it is in the sense of «it says: the people…».

nahhas-irab:87-87.t:
وَيَوْمَ يُنْفَخُ فِي الصُّورِ: in the sense of «and remember». The doctrine of al-Farrāʾ is that the meaning is «and that is the day the Trumpet is blown», and he permitted omission in it, and made it like وَلَوْ تَرى إِذْ فَزِعُوا فَلا فَوْتَ [Sabaʾ: 51].
فَفَزِعَ مَنْ فِي السَّماواتِ وَمَنْ فِي الْأَرْضِ: this is a past verb, while «ينفخ» is future; so it is asked: how can a past be conjoined to a future? Al-Farrāʾ claimed that it is construed according to the meaning, because the meaning is «when the Trumpet is blown, then [all] are terrified». إِلَّا مَنْ شاءَ اللَّهُ: in the position of the accusative as an exception (istithnāʾ). The Medinans, Abū ʿAmr, ʿĀṣim and al-Kisāʾī read «وكلّ آتوه داخرين», making it a future [form] [Translator's note: i.e. the active participle «آتُوهُ»], and al-Aʿmash and Ḥamza read وَكُلٌّ أَتَوْهُ, making it a past verb. Abū Jaʿfar said: in my book from Abū Isḥāq on the Qurʾān [it says]: whoever reads وَكُلٌّ أَتَوْهُ used the singular according to the wording of «كلّ», and whoever reads آتَوْهُ used the plural according to its meaning.
This statement is an ugly error, because if one says «وكلّ أتوه», he has not used the singular but rather the plural; had he used the singular he would have said
«أتاه». Rather, whoever says «أتوه» used the plural according to the meaning and brought it as a past because he referred it back to «ففزع»; and whoever reads «وكلّ آتوه» construed it according to the meaning, and said «آتوه» because it is a clause cut off from the first.

nahhas-irab:88-88.t: وَتَرَى الْجِبالَ: from seeing with the eye; were it from seeing with the heart (i.e. knowing), it would take two objects. The origin is «ترأى»: the vowel of the hamza was thrown onto the rāʾ, so the rāʾ became vowelled and the hamza was dropped. This is the way of lightening the hamza when a quiescent letter precedes it, except that the lightening is obligatory for «ترى» and its fellow imperfect forms because of its frequency in speech, and because it is used for seeing with the eye and with the heart. تَحْسَبُها جامِدَةً: «تحسب» must have two objects, whereas «ظننت» is sometimes transitive to only one. The people of Kufa read تَحْسَبُها [with fatḥa], and that is the analogical form, because it is from ḥasiba yaḥsabu; but it has been reported from the Prophet ﷺ contrary to this, that he read with kasra in the imperfect, so it is on the pattern faʿila yafʿilu, as they said naʿima yanʿimu and yaʾisa yayʾisu; and baʾisa yabʾisu has been reported among the sound verbs. Nothing besides these words is known in the speech of the Arabs. وَهِيَ تَمُرُّ مَرَّ السَّحابِ: a maṣdar (verbal noun); its implied form is «a passing like the passing of the clouds»: you put the adjective in place of the qualified noun and the muḍāf ilayhi [in place of the muḍāf]. صُنْعَ اللَّهِ: accusative according to al-Khalīl and Sībawayh, may Allah have mercy on them both, as a maṣdar, because when He, Mighty and Majestic, said «وهي تمرّ مرّ السّحاب», this indicated that He made that a making. The accusative is also permissible as incitement (ighrāʾ), i.e. «look at the making of Allah». Abū Isḥāq said: the nominative is also permissible, in the sense of «that is the making of Allah».

nahhas-irab:89-89.t:
وَهُمْ مِنْ فَزَعٍ يَوْمَئِذٍ آمِنُونَ: you put «يوم» in the genitive by annexation (iḍāfa) and drop the tanwīn for it. Whoever puts it in the accusative while annexing, reading مِنْ فَزَعٍ يَوْمَئِذٍ آمِنُونَ [Translator's note: printed with the same vowelling; the reading meant is «مِنْ فَزَعِ يَوْمَئِذٍ» with «يومَئذ» indeclinable], makes «يومئذ» indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, being annexed to something non-declinable. Sībawayh recited: [al-Ṭawīl] 323-
على حين ألهى النّاس جلّ أمورهم
(At a time when the greater part of their affairs had distracted people.)
If someone says: Sībawayh said: «tanwīn is, in their view, the sign of the most declinable (al-amkan)», and he said: «and they are far from resemblance [to the verb], as far as كم and إذ are from the declinable words» — then how can tanwīn be the sign of the most declinable and then enter what is in no way declinable? This is a kind of contradiction. The answer to this is that the tanwīn Sībawayh meant is not this tanwīn; rather, whoever imagines so was weak in Arabic. The tanwīn he meant is that of which some grammarians say: it was introduced to distinguish between what is fully declined and what is a diptote; and some of them say: to distinguish between noun and verb. Tanwīn has two other kinds: it may distinguish between definite and indefinite, and it may be a compensation (ʿiwaḍ), as in your saying «جوار» and in your saying «يومئذ».

nahhas-irab:90-90.t: The verb from this is «كبّه» (he overturned it), and the intransitive from it is «أكبّ», and this rarely occurs in the speech of the Arabs.

nahhas-irab:91-91.t: إِنَّما أُمِرْتُ أَنْ أَعْبُدَ رَبَّ هذِهِ الْبَلْدَةِ الَّذِي حَرَّمَها وَلَهُ كُلُّ شَيْءٍ وَأُمِرْتُ أَنْ أَكُونَ مِنَ الْمُسْلِمِينَ (91): الَّذِي is in the position of the accusative as a naʿt (adjective) of «رب». Had it been with the alif and lām, you would say «المحرّمها». If it were an adjective of «البلدة», [you would say] «المحرّمها هو»: the pronoun must be made overt with the alif and lām, because the [participle] runs on something other than the one it belongs to. If you say «الذي حرّمها», you have no need to say «هو».

nahhas-irab:92-92.t:
وَأَنْ أَتْلُوَا: accusative by «أن». Al-Farrāʾ said: in one of the two readings it is «وأن اتل القرآن», and he claimed it is in the position of the jussive by the command, which is why the wāw was dropped from it. Abū Jaʿfar said:
we know of no one who read with this reading, and it contradicts all the codices. His saying that it is in the position of the jussive is an error according to the Basrans, because there is no jussive without a jussive-governing word. And to imply the lām is an error: it would have been necessary to bring the prefix of the imperfect, so how can the lām be implied, when if it were brought the speech would be otherwise? And the jussive particles are not implied. This verb [the imperative] cannot be declinable (muʿrab), because it is not the imperfect. Sībawayh said: they made it quiescent because it is not used as a qualifier and does not occur in the position of the imperfect.

nahhas-irab:93-93.t: وَما رَبُّكَ بِغافِلٍ عَمَّا تَعْمَلُونَ: with tāʾ so that the speech is on one consistent pattern; and with yāʾ on the basis of referring it back to what precedes it, or of a shift in address (from second to third person).

nahhas-irab:1-1.t: «طس تِلْكَ آياتُ الْقُرْآنِ», in the sense of "these are those verses of the Qur'an". What is permissible in the beginning of «البقرة», in His saying, Mighty and Majestic, «ذلِكَ الْكِتابُ» [al-Baqara: 2], is permissible in this. «وَكِتابٍ مُبِينٍ» is conjoined to «القرآن». Abū Isḥāq [al-Zajjāj] said: «وكتابٌ مبين» [in the nominative] is also permissible, in the sense of "and that is a clear Book".

nahhas-irab:2-2.t: «هُدىً» is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), and what is permissible elsewhere, at the beginning of Sūrat «البقرة», in His saying, Mighty and Majestic, «هُدىً لِلْمُتَّقِينَ» [al-Baqara: 2], is permissible in it.

nahhas-irab:3-3.t: «الَّذِينَ يُقِيمُونَ الصَّلاةَ» is in the position of the nominative on the basis of an implied mubtadaʾ (subject), and what is permissible at the beginning of Sūrat «البقرة», in His saying, Mighty and Majestic, «الَّذِينَ يُؤْمِنُونَ بِالْغَيْبِ» [al-Baqara: 3], is permissible in it.

nahhas-irab:4-4.t: «إِنَّ الَّذِينَ لا يُؤْمِنُونَ بِالْآخِرَةِ»: [«الذين»] is the noun of «إنّ». «زَيَّنَّا لَهُمْ أَعْمالَهُمْ» is in the position of the khabar (predicate).

nahhas-irab:5-5.t: «أُوْلئِكَ» is in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and its khabar (predicate) is «الَّذِينَ لَهُمْ سُوءُ الْعَذابِ»; one also says «الّذون» in the position of the nominative. «وَهُمْ فِي الْآخِرَةِ هُمُ الْأَخْسَرُونَ»: «فِي الْآخِرَةِ» is an explanation (tabyīn) and is not attached to «الأخسرين».

nahhas-irab:6-7.t:
«لَدُنْ» means "with" (عند), except that it is indeclinable (mabnī), not declined, because it is not fully nominal (lā tatamakkan).
The Medinans and Abū ʿAmr read «بشهابِ قبسٍ» [in construct], and the Kufans read «بِشِهابٍ قَبَسٍ» [with tanwīn]. Al-Farrāʾ claimed, regarding the omission of the tanwīn, that it is like their saying «وَلَدارُ الْآخِرَةِ» [Yūsuf: 109]: a thing is put in construct with itself when its names differ. Abū Jaʿfar said: putting a thing in construct with itself is impossible according to the Basrans,
because the meaning of the construct (al-iḍāfa) in the language is joining a thing [to another] so as to make clear by it the sense of possession or kind; and it is impossible to make clear that it possesses itself or is of its own kind. «بشهاب قبس» is putting the kind in construct with the body, as you say هذا ثوب خزّ ("this is a garment of silk"). Al-shihāb is anything possessing light, such as a star or a burning stick; al-qabas is a name for what is taken [as a light] from embers and the like; so the meaning is "with a flame of firebrand". One says
قبست قبسا ("I took a light"), and the noun is قبس, just as you say قبض قبضا and the noun is القبض. Whoever reads «بشهابٍ قبسٍ» makes it a badal (substitute). «بشهاب قبسا» is permissible outside the Qur'an, as a maṣdar (verbal noun), an explanation (bayān) or a ḥāl (circumstantial). «لَعَلَّكُمْ تَصْطَلُونَ»: the original of the ṭāʾ is tāʾ, and ṭāʾ was substituted for it because the ṭāʾ is velarised (muṭbaqa) and the ṣād is velarised, so joining them was good.

nahhas-irab:8-8.t: Abū Isḥāq [al-Zajjāj] said: «أن» is in the position of the accusative, i.e. "[He called] that". [Translator's note: «أي بأنه "قال"» is translated as printed; the sense appears to be "i.e. by that", with something garbled in the source.] It may also be in the position of the nominative, making it the deputy agent (nāʾib fāʿil) of the passive verb. Abū Ḥātim related that in the reading of Ubayy, Ibn ʿAbbās and Mujāhid there is «أن بوركت النار ومن حولها» ("that the fire and those around it were blessed"); something like this is not found with a sound chain of transmission, and even if it were sound, it would be by way of exegesis. Saʿīd related from Qatāda: «أن بورك من في النّار ومن حولها» — he said: the angels. Al-Kisāʾī related from the Arabs: باركك الله and بارك فيك ("may Allah bless you").

nahhas-irab:10-10.t: «فَلَمَّا رَآها تَهْتَزُّ»: [«تهتزّ»] is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). «كَأَنَّها جَانٌّ»: al-jānn among the Arabs is the thuʿbān, which is the huge snake. «وَلَّى مُدْبِراً»: as a ḥāl. «وَلَمْ يُعَقِّبْ»: Qatāda said: i.e. he did not turn round. «يا مُوسى لا تَخَفْ», i.e. it was said to him: do not fear the snake and its harm. «إِنِّي لا يَخافُ لَدَيَّ الْمُرْسَلُونَ»: this is the end of the sentence.

nahhas-irab:11-11.t:
«إِلَّا مَنْ ظَلَمَ ثُمَّ بَدَّلَ حُسْناً بَعْدَ سُوءٍ» is an exception not of the same kind as the first, in the position of the accusative. Al-Farrāʾ claimed that the exception is from something omitted, the meaning in his view being: "Truly, in My presence the messengers do not fear; only others fear — except whoever has done wrong and then substituted good after evil, for he does not fear". Al-Farrāʾ also claimed that some grammarians make «إلّا» mean "and" (wāw). Abū Jaʿfar said: an exception from something omitted is impossible, because it is an exception from something not mentioned; if this were permissible, then إنّي أضرب القوم إلّا زيدا ("I strike the people except Zayd") would be permissible in the sense of "I do not strike the people; I only strike others, except Zayd" — and this is the opposite of clear expression, and bringing what has no recognisable meaning. As for «إلّا» meaning "and", there is no justification for it, and it is not permissible in any speech. The meaning of «إلّا» is the opposite of the meaning of "and", because when you say جاءني إخوتك إلّا زيدا ("your brothers came to me except Zayd"), you have excluded Zayd from what the brothers were included in; and when you say جاءني إخوتك وزيد ("your brothers and Zayd came to me"), you have included Zayd in what the brothers were included in. So there is no resemblance or nearness between them. There is a third view on the verse: the meaning would be that when Moses ﷺ feared the snake and He, Mighty and Majestic, said to him «لا تَخَفْ إِنِّي لا يَخافُ لَدَيَّ الْمُرْسَلُونَ», He, Mighty and Majestic, knew that whoever among them had disobeyed would harbour fear secretly, so He excepted him and said: "except whoever has done wrong and then substituted good after evil", i.e. for he will fear, even though I have forgiven him. If someone says: what is the meaning of fear after repentance and forgiveness? It is said to him: this is the way of those who know Allah, Mighty and Majestic — that they are fearful of [having committed] acts of disobedience to Him, and apprehensive; and also they are not secure that some condition of repentance may have remained which they did not fulfil, so they fear being called to account for it. Mujāhid read «ثُمَّ بَدَّلَ حُسْناً بَعْدَ سُوءٍ» [i.e. حَسَنا, "something good"]. Abū Jaʿfar said:
This is far-fetched in more than one respect: among them, that he put the adjective in place of the thing qualified in something shared [by several things]; and among them, that the pairing of the speech would be "substituted good after bad (sayyiʾ)". Though some have recited Zuhayr's verse: [al-basīṭ] 316-
يطلب شأو امرأين قدّما حسنا ... فاقا الملوك وبذّا هذه السّوقا
(He seeks to reach the goal of two men who sent forth good deeds, who surpassed kings and outstripped these common folk.)

nahhas-irab:12-12.t:
«تَخْرُجْ بَيْضاءَ مِنْ غَيْرِ سُوءٍ»: «تخرج» is jussive because it is the answer to the imperative, and it carries the sense of requital.
«فِي تِسْعِ آياتٍ»: the best thing said about it is that the meaning is: this sign is included among nine signs.

nahhas-irab:13-13.t: «فَلَمَّا جاءَتْهُمْ آياتُنا مُبْصِرَةً» is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). Abū Isḥāq [al-Zajjāj] said: «مبصَرة» is also permissible, i.e. made clear, seen. Al-Akhfash said: «مَبصَرة» is also permissible as a maṣdar (verbal noun), just as one says «الولد مجبنة» ("a child is a cause of cowardice").

nahhas-irab:16-16.t: Saʿīd said, from Qatāda, [on] «وَوَرِثَ سُلَيْمانُ داوُدَ»: he said: he inherited prophethood and kingship from him ﷺ. «وَقالَ يا أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ عُلِّمْنا مَنْطِقَ الطَّيْرِ»: [«منطق»] is the [second object standing as] predicate of the passive verb. «المنطق» may apply to what is understood without speech; and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, knows best what He meant.

nahhas-irab:17-17.t: It is said that the jinn were subjected to him because he controlled what was harmful and beneficial in them; and the birds were subjected to him in that there was placed in them what understood him, so they would shade him from the sun and other things. It has been said: for this reason he inspected [lit. "missed"] the hoopoe.

nahhas-irab:18-18.t: What is said about [the ant's] speech is as has passed on «المنطق». «يا أَيُّهَا النَّمْلُ ادْخُلُوا مَساكِنَكُمْ»: it comes in the form of addressing human beings, since they [the ants] are reported about with the reports of human beings. «لا يَحْطِمَنَّكُمْ» may be a prohibition, or an answer [to the command]; the nūn is for emphasis.

nahhas-irab:20-20.t:
«وَتَفَقَّدَ الطَّيْرَ فَقالَ ما لِيَ لا أَرَى الْهُدْهُدَ»: this is the reading of the Medinans and Abū ʿAmr, with sukūn on the yāʾ [i.e. ما لِيْ], while they read «وما لِيَ لا أعبد الذي فطرني» [Yā Sīn: 22] with a vowel on the yāʾ. Some people claimed that they wanted to distinguish between what is at the beginning [of a sentence] and what is conjoined to what precedes it. Abū Jaʿfar said:
This is nothing; it is simply the yāʾ of the first person: some Arabs give it fatḥa and some give it sukūn, and they read with both dialect forms. The proof of this is that a group of the great readers read both with fatḥa — among them ʿAbdallāh ibn Kathīr, ʿĀṣim and al-Kisāʾī — and that Ḥamza read both with sukūn. The eloquent form of the first-person yāʾ is for it to have fatḥa, because it is a noun consisting of a single letter, so the preferred choice is that it not be made quiescent, which would curtail the noun. «أَمْ كانَ مِنَ الْغائِبِينَ», in the sense of "or rather" (أبل).

nahhas-irab:21-21.t: «لَأُعَذِّبَنَّهُ عَذاباً شَدِيداً أَوْ لَأَذْبَحَنَّهُ» is emphasised with the heavy nūn; it and the light [nūn] are obligatory [here]. Abū Ḥātim said: had it been read «لَأُعَذِّبَنْهُ عَذاباً شَدِيداً أَوْ لَأَذْبَحَنْهُ» [with the light nūn], it would be permissible. [Translator's note: the variant is printed identically to the canonical text in the source; the light-nūn form is meant.] «أَوْ لَيَأْتِيَنِّي بِسُلْطانٍ مُبِينٍ»: this may be the light nūn, then assimilated into the nūn that goes with the yāʾ; or the nūn that goes with the yāʾ may have been dropped, as one says إنّي ذاهب, and it is emphasised with the heavy [nūn]. The people of Mecca read «أو ليأتينّني».

nahhas-irab:22-22.t:
«فَمَكَثَ غَيْرَ بَعِيدٍ» is the reading of ʿĀṣim, and it is related from al-Aʿmash; the reading of the rest of the readers is «فَمَكَثَ» [i.e. فمكُث, with ḍamma]. [Translator's note: «قراء عاصم» is translated as «قراءة عاصم», which is evidently meant; both readings are printed identically in the source.] Sībawayh said: مكث يمكث مكوثا, just as they said قعد يقعد قعودا. He said:
and مكُث is like ظرُف; the argument of whoever reads with ḍamma, according to Sībawayh, is that it is intransitive, like ظرُف. Abū Jaʿfar said:
I heard ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān say: the proof that مكَث is more eloquent is their saying ماكث, while they do not say «مكث» — so this differs from ظرُف [whose participle is ظريف]. Abū Jaʿfar said: this is a clear argument, because faʿula with the participle fāʿil is not known in the speech of the Arabs except in things disputed, some of which are rejected. As for those that are disputed: طلقت المرأة فهي طالق ("the woman was divorced, so she is divorced"), and it has also been said طلُقت; and حمض الخلّ فهو حامض ("the vinegar turned sour, so it is sour"), and it has also been said حمُض. Abū Ḥātim claimed that in their saying فره فهو فاره there is no disagreement.
So he said; but others have related فره يفره فهو فره وفاره, like حذر — Quṭrub related this. «غَيْرَ بَعِيدٍ»: Abū Isḥāq [al-Zajjāj] said: i.e. a time not far off. «فَقالَ أَحَطْتُ بِما لَمْ تُحِطْ بِهِ»: in this there is a refutation of whoever says that the prophets know the unseen. Al-Farrāʾ related (أحطّ), assimilating the tāʾ into the ṭāʾ, and related أحتّ, changing the ṭāʾ into tāʾ and assimilating. «وجئتك من سبإٍ بنبإ يقين» is the reading of the Medinans and the Kufans. The Meccans and the Basrans read «مِنْ سَبَإٍ بِنَبَإٍ يَقِينٍ» [i.e. من سبأَ] without declension (as a diptote). Al-Farrāʾ claimed that al-Ruʾāsī asked Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ, may Allah have mercy on him, about «سبأ», and he said: "I do not know what it is." Al-Farrāʾ interpreted Abū ʿAmr as having made it a diptote because it is unknown, and [held] that when a thing is not known it is not declined, and he adduced as proof [the poet's] saying: [al-ṭawīl] 317-
يكن ما أساء النّار في رأس كبكبا
(Whatever wrong he did will be [as conspicuous as] the fire on the top of Kabkab.)
Abū ʿAmr is too eminent to say something like this, and there is no proof in al-Ruʾāsī's report from him that he made it a diptote only because he did not know it; he only said "I do not know it". If a grammarian were asked about a noun and said "I do not know it", that would be no proof that he makes it a diptote; rather the truth is otherwise: what is required when you do not know it is to decline it, because the basic rule of nouns is declension, and a thing is made a diptote only for a cause entering upon it; so the basic rule stands and is not removed by something unknown. His argument from «كبكب» has no sense, because Kabkab is a well-known mountain, made a diptote because it is a place, even though declining it is good. The proof of what we said is that Abū ʿAmr argued only from the speech of the Arabs, and did not argue that he did not know it; he recited [the verse] of al-Nābigha al-Jaʿdī: [al-munsariḥ] 318-
من سبأ الحاضرين مأرب إذ ... يبنون من دون سيله العرما
(Of Sabaʾ, those dwelling at Maʾrib, when they built the dam against its flood.)
Though Abū ʿAmr was opposed on this: it was related «من سبأٍ الحاضرين…», with the tanwīn dropped because of the meeting of two quiescent letters. Abū Jaʿfar said: I heard ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān say: I heard Muḥammad ibn Yazīd [al-Mubarrad] say: I heard ʿUmāra read «وَلَا اللَّيْلُ سابِقُ» [Yā Sīn: 40] with the accusative [i.e. سابقُ النهارَ], dropping the tanwīn because of the meeting of two quiescent letters. Abū ʿUbayd al-Qāsim ibn Sallām spoke on this with a discourse full of confusion, and we dictate it in the exact wording of what he said, since his book is one of the source works, so that the exact wording of what he said may be seen and the place of the mistake in it known. Abū ʿUbayd said: it is our reading which we choose — meaning «من سبأَ بنبإ يقين». Abū ʿUbayd said: because «سبأ» is a feminine name, of a woman or of a tribe, and it is not light so as to be declined for its lightness; whoever declines it takes it to be the name of a man, and whoever holds this is obliged to decline «ثمود» throughout the Qur'an, for although today it is the name of a tribe, it was originally the name of a man, and likewise «سبأ». If it is said that «ثمود» is greater in number [of letters] than «سبأ» by one letter, it is replied that the vowel on the bāʾ and the hamza have added to its heaviness more than that letter or as much as it; the addition in «ثمود» is only a quiescent wāw. Abū Jaʿfar said: his saying "because «سبأ» is a feminine name, of a woman or of a tribe" implies that he left it undeclined for one of these two reasons, and the one does not resemble the other, because the name of a woman is real feminine and the name of a tribe is unreal feminine; and the choice according to Sībawayh for names of tribes, when «بنو» is not used with them, is declension, as with «ثمود». His saying "it is not light so as to be declined for its lightness" is no proof against whoever declines it, because no one we know has said "I declined it because it is light". His saying "whoever declines it takes it to be the name of a man" is not the argument of whoever declines it; his argument is only that it is a name for the clan, even if its origin in reality is the name of a man. Farwa ibn Musayk and ʿAbdallāh ibn ʿAbbās related from the Prophet ﷺ — and it is well known in genealogy — "Sabaʾ ibn Yashjub ibn Yaʿrub ibn Qaḥṭān". Abū Isḥāq [al-Zajjāj], however, claimed that whoever declines it makes it the name of the land. And his saying "If it is said that «ثمود» is greater in number than «سبأ», it is replied that the two vowels on the bāʾ and the hamza have added to its heaviness more than that letter or as much as it" — this is the place of confusion, because [comparing] the vowel on the bāʾ and the hamza in «ثمود» and «سبأ» by vowelling has no sense, since both of them are vowelled. Abū Jaʿfar said: the [right] view on «سبأ» is what authoritative report has brought, that it was originally the name of a man. If you decline it, it is because it has become a name for the clan; and if you do not decline it, you make it a name for the tribe, like «ثمود»; except that the choice according to Sībawayh is declension, and his argument for that is decisive, because since this name applies to both masculine and feminine, the masculine is preferable, as it is the original and the lighter.

nahhas-irab:24-25.t:
«وَزَيَّنَ لَهُمُ الشَّيْطانُ أَعْمالَهُمْ فَصَدَّهُمْ عَنِ السَّبِيلِ فَهُمْ لا يَهْتَدُونَ أَلَّا يَسْجُدُوا لِلَّهِ»: this is the reading of Abū ʿAmr, ʿĀṣim, Nāfiʿ and Ḥamza. Al-Zuhrī, Abū Jaʿfar, Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, Ḥumayd, Ṭalḥa and al-Kisāʾī read «ألا يا اسجدوا لله» ("Lo! O [you], prostrate to Allah"). In the first reading, it is «أن» with «لا» entering on it, in the position of the accusative. [Translator's note: «هي أن دخلت عليها "وإن"» is translated in the sense evidently intended; the printed text is garbled.] Al-Akhfash said: the meaning is "so that they do not prostrate". Al-Kisāʾī said:
the meaning is "so he barred them from prostrating". ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān said: «أن» is a badal (substitute) for «أعمالهم», in the position of the accusative. It has been said: its position is genitive as a badal for «السبيل». The second reading is in the sense of "Lo! O you, prostrate", as [the poet] said: [al-ṭawīl] 319-
ألا يا اسلمي يا دارمي على البلى ... ولا زال منهلّا بجرعائك القطر
(Lo! O be safe, O abode of Mayya, despite decay, and may the rain never cease pouring on your sandy ground.)
And another said: [al-basīṭ] 320-
يا لعنة الله والأقوام كلّهم ... والصّالحين على سمعان من جار
(O — the curse of Allah, of all peoples and of the righteous, be upon Simʿān, what a neighbour!)
The meaning is: "O you, the curse of Allah…". Abū Jaʿfar said: this is found in the speech of the Arabs, except that it is not usual to say يا قدم زيد ("O, Zayd came"), and reading with it is remote, because the speech becomes parenthetical, whereas with the first reading the speech is well ordered. Moreover, the written text (al-sawād) is not according to this reading, because two alifs would have been omitted from it, while something like this is abbreviated only by omitting a single alif, as in «يا عِيسَى ابْنَ مَرْيَمَ» [al-Māʾida:
110]. «الَّذِي يُخْرِجُ الْخَبْءَ فِي السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ»: the pause on it is with sukūn on the hamza; and when it is in the position of the nominative, rawm and ishmām [partial vowel indication in pause] are permissible, but doubling is not permissible. Abū Ḥātim related that ʿIkrima read «الّذي يخرج الخبا في السماوات والأرض» with an alif without hamza, and he claimed that this is not permissible in Arabic, arguing that if one lightened the hamza one would throw its vowel onto the bāʾ and drop it, and say «الخبَ في السّموات», and that if one converted the hamza one would say «الخبي», with sukūn on the bāʾ followed by yāʾ. Abū Jaʿfar said: [as for] his saying that «الخبا» is not permissible — I heard ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān say: I heard Muḥammad ibn Yazīd [al-Mubarrad] say: he — meaning Abū Ḥātim — was below his colleagues in grammar and did not reach their level, except that when he left his town he met no one more learned than he. Sībawayh related from the Arabs that they substitute alif for the hamza when a quiescent letter precedes it and it has fatḥa, wāw when a quiescent letter precedes it and it has ḍamma, and yāʾ when a quiescent letter precedes it and it has kasra; and that one says هذا الوثو, عجبت من الوثى and رأيت الوثا — from وثئت يده ("his hand was sprained") — and likewise هذا الخبو, عجبت من الخبي and رأيت الخبا. This is done only because the hamza is lightened, so these letters are substituted for it.
Sībawayh related from some people of Banū Tamīm and Banū Asad that they say هذا الخبُوء: they give ḍamma to the quiescent letter when the hamza has ḍamma, and they keep the hamza and give kasra to the quiescent letter when the hamza has kasra, and fatḥa to the quiescent letter when the hamza has fatḥa. Sībawayh also related that they give kasra even when the hamza has ḍamma — but this is from Banū Tamīm — and they say هذا الرّدِي; and he claimed that they did not give ḍamma to the dāl because they disliked a ḍamma preceded by a kasra, since there is no fiʿul pattern in the language.
All of these are dialect forms entering upon the dialect in which the community [of readers] read.

nahhas-irab:28-28.t: «اذْهَبْ بِكِتابِي هذا فَأَلْقِهْ إِلَيْهِمْ»: Abū Isḥāq [al-Zajjāj] said: there are five ways [of reading] it: (فألقهي إليهم), with the yāʾ pronounced; with the yāʾ dropped and the kasra kept to indicate it (فألقهِ إليهم); with ḍamma on the hāʾ and the wāw kept according to the original (فألقهو إليهم); with the wāw dropped and the ḍamma kept (فألقهُ إليهم); and the fifth dialect form, which Ḥamza read, with sukūn on the hāʾ (فألقهْ إليهم). According to the grammarians this is not permissible except by a far-fetched device, namely that the pause is supposed. I heard ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān say: pay no attention to this form; if it were permissible to continue while intending the pause, it would be permissible to drop the case-endings from nouns.

nahhas-irab:30-30.t: I.e. "and [it says] that the speech", or "that the beginning of the speech is «بسم الله الرّحمن الرّحيم»". Al-Farrāʾ permitted «إِنَّهُ مِنْ سُلَيْمانَ وَإِنَّهُ» with fatḥa on both [i.e. أنّه … وأنّه], on the basis that they are in the position of the nominative, in the sense of "it was cast to me that it is from Solomon"; and he permitted that they be in the position of the accusative by omission of the preposition.

nahhas-irab:31-31.t: «أَلَّا تَعْلُوا عَلَيَّ»: Abū Isḥāq [al-Zajjāj] mentioned three ways for «أن»: it may be in the position of the accusative in the sense of "with [the message] that"; it may be in the position of the nominative in the sense of "it was cast to me that"; and the third way is that it be in the sense of "that is" (أي), like «وَانْطَلَقَ الْمَلَأُ مِنْهُمْ أَنِ امْشُوا» [Ṣād: 6], the meaning being "that is: walk on", and "they said: walk on". Likewise «ألّا تعلوا عليّ», i.e. he said: do not exalt yourselves against me. It is related from Wahb ibn Munabbih that he read «ألّا تغلوا عليّ», from غلا يغلو, when one goes beyond bounds. «وَأْتُونِي مُسْلِمِينَ» is written without yāʾ, because the wāw is not joined [to what follows].

nahhas-irab:32-32.t: «قالَتْ يا أَيُّهَا الْمَلَأُ أَفْتُونِي»: with lightening of the second hamza is the eloquent form. If you wish, you may lighten the first alone; if you wish, you may lighten both; and if you wish, you may pronounce both fully — which is the most remote of the forms because of the heaviness of combining two hamzas. «ما كُنْتُ قاطِعَةً أَمْراً حَتَّى تَشْهَدُونِ»: the nūn [of the indicative] was dropped for the subjunctive, and the yāʾ was dropped because the kasra indicates it, and the nūn goes with the verb, and it is a verse-end. Fatḥa on the nūn is not permissible; if it were so, the verb would be indicative.

nahhas-irab:33-34.t: «أُولُوا»: this is a collective noun, and its singular is ذو. Al-Aʿmash related from Mujāhid; he said: under her command were twelve thousand chiefs (qayl), and under the command of each chief a hundred thousand. She answered them on this: «إِنَّ الْمُلُوكَ إِذا دَخَلُوا قَرْيَةً أَفْسَدُوها», i.e. by force, i.e. by subjugation and conquest, «وَجَعَلُوا أَعِزَّةَ أَهْلِها أَذِلَّةً». Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: «وَكَذلِكَ يَفْعَلُونَ» — this is not part of her speech; so said Saʿīd ibn Jubayr.

nahhas-irab:35-35.t:
«وَإِنِّي مُرْسِلَةٌ إِلَيْهِمْ بِهَدِيَّةٍ»: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr said, from Ibn ʿAbbās: she sent them a brick of gold, or gold; the messengers saw [lit. "read"] the walls of gold, and what they had brought became small in their eyes. She said
«مرسلة إليهم» while it was only to Solomon ﷺ, as is reported of kings: they are addressed [in the plural] and they address [in the plural]. It has been said that the gift was something other than this, except that his saying «أتمدّونني بمال» indicates this. «فَناظِرَةٌ بِمَ يَرْجِعُ الْمُرْسَلُونَ»: the original is «بما»; the alif was dropped to distinguish between the question and the statement. This happens only when a preposition precedes «ما». In a statement you say رغبت فيما عندك ("I desired what you have"), keeping the alif in «فيما» and nothing else; and in a question you say فيم نظرت؟ ("into what did you look?"), dropping the alif. Al-Farrāʾ permitted keeping it in the question, and this is one of the irregularities against which the Qur'an has come.
